ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two platforms, separated by a distance of $L=11.5m$, are located on the same horizontal plane and are connected by a conveyor belt. The conveyor belt moves uniformly to the right, and its velocity magnitude $v$ can be set by the drive system as needed. A cargo box (which can be treated as a point mass) with a mass of $m=10{kg}$ slides onto the conveyor belt from the left platform with an initial velocity of $v_{0}=5.0{m/s}$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the cargo box and the conveyor belt is $\mu=0.10$, and the acceleration due to gravity is taken as $g=10\mathsf{m}/\mathsf{s}^{2}$.

1. If $v=4.0\mathsf{m/s}$, determine the time required for the cargo box to traverse the conveyor belt.
2. Determine the maximum and minimum velocities that the cargo box can attain when it reaches the right platform.
3. If $v=6.0\mathsf{m/s}$, after the cargo box slides onto the conveyor belt for $\Delta t=\frac{13}{12}{s}$, the velocity of the conveyor belt suddenly becomes zero. Determine the impulse exerted by the conveyor belt on the cargo box during its motion from the left platform to the right platform.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left and right platforms are on the same horizontal line, and the middle is connected by the upper surface of a conveyor belt; the cargo box on the left platform enters the conveyor belt to the right with the marked initial velocity v0; the distance L is marked above the conveyor belt, representing the horizontal distance that the cargo box passes between the platforms at the two ends; the arrow of the conveyor belt speed v also points to the right. Take the rightward direction as the positive direction. When relative sliding occurs between the cargo box and the conveyor belt, the magnitude of kinetic friction is f=μmg, so the magnitude of the horizontal acceleration of the cargo box is a=μg=0.10×10=1 m/s^2. If the velocity of the cargo box is greater than the belt speed, the friction force is leftward and the acceleration is -1 m/s^2; if the velocity of the cargo box is less than the belt speed, the friction force is rightward and the acceleration is +1 m/s^2. 1. When v=4.0 m/s, the initial v0=5.0 m/s, which is greater than the belt speed, so the cargo box first decelerates: the time used to decrease from 5 m/s to 4 m/s is t1=(5-4)/1=1 s. The displacement in this stage is s1=((5+4)/2)×1=4.5 m. The remaining displacement is 11.5-4.5=7.0 m. Afterwards, the cargo box has the same speed as the conveyor belt and moves forward uniformly at 4 m/s, using time t2=7.0/4=1.75 s. The total time is t=t1+t2=2.75 s. 2. The velocity of the cargo box when reaching the right platform is maximum: choose a sufficiently large belt speed so that the velocity of the cargo box is less than the belt speed throughout the whole process, the friction force is always rightward, and the acceleration is +1 m/s^2. From vf^2=v0^2+2aL=5^2+2×1×11.5=48, obtain vmax=√48=4√3 m/s. The velocity of the cargo box when reaching the right platform is minimum: choose a sufficiently small belt speed so that the velocity of the cargo box is greater than the belt speed throughout the whole process, the friction force is always leftward, and the acceleration is -1 m/s^2. From vf^2=v0^2-2aL=5^2-2×1×11.5=2, obtain vmin=√2 m/s. 3. When the initial belt speed v=6.0 m/s, the initial speed of the cargo box is 5 m/s, less than the belt speed, so it first accelerates under rightward friction. The time used to accelerate from 5 m/s to 6 m/s is 1 s, and the displacement is s1=((5+6)/2)×1=5.5 m. The problem states that after Δt=13/12 s the conveyor belt suddenly stops, so between the 1st s and the 13/12 s, the cargo box has the same speed as the conveyor belt, 6 m/s, moves for a total of 1/12 s, and has displacement s2=6×(1/12)=0.5 m. At this time it has already traveled 6.0 m, and 11.5-6.0=5.5 m remains. After the conveyor belt stops, the cargo box still moves rightward with speed 6 m/s, slides rightward relative to the conveyor belt, the friction force is leftward, and the acceleration is -1 m/s^2. After traveling the remaining 5.5 m, the final velocity satisfies vf^2=6^2-2×1×5.5=25, so vf=5 m/s, and the time used in this stage is t3=(6-5)/1=1 s. The total contact time is T=13/12+1=25/12 s. Horizontal friction impulse: the acceleration stage in the first 1 s is m(6-5)=10 N·s; the deceleration stage after the conveyor belt stops is m(5-6)=-10 N·s; the horizontal friction in the middle same-speed stage is zero. Therefore the horizontal impulses cancel each other, and the total horizontal impulse is 0. In the vertical direction, the impulse is provided by the supporting force of the conveyor belt, with magnitude JN=mgT=10×10×(25/12)=2500/12≈208.3 N·s, direction vertically upward. Therefore, the total impulse of the conveyor belt on the cargo box is 208.3 N·s, direction vertically upward.
